author: canonical_scout_r68
body:
# Canonical population reuse design scout

## Owner map

`proofir_v3.validate_envelope(value)` remains the one-envelope raw API: it canonical-encodes, reparses into owned JSON, runs semantic validation, and returns a frozen `ProofIRV3Artifact`; its public return object's `to_dict()` intentionally returns a detached mutable copy. `validate_envelope_batch(values)` is the raw full-batch API. `proofir_v3_batch.preflight()` visits every original occurrence, calls `_prepare_envelope`, totals every occurrence's bytes, and rejects over-limit batches / same-ID-different-content before building the ID map. It then validates cross-artifact refs against that map, which is deduplicated by ID, and returns validated artifacts in original occurrence order.

The dossier route is `result_inspection.inspect_result_manifest` -> `result_dossier.prepare_dossier` -> `result_resolution.resolve_result_targets` -> `result_resolution._catalog`. `_catalog` calls `validate_envelope_batch(artifacts)`, converts each validated row to a fresh dict, then builds an ID-keyed catalog (so same-ID/same-bytes occurrences collapse only after batch accounting). `result_inspection_checks.checking_cards` walks all catalog check-runs (including checks off the selected page) and eagerly calls `_receipt` for each; its `_input_environments` selects exact input environment artifact rows from the complete catalog. `stored_check_receipt` currently revalidates the raw check with `validate_envelope(dict(artifact))`; with recorded toolchain context, `validate_recorded_execution_binding` calls `validate_envelope_batch([dict(environment), dict(check)])`. This pair check is deliberately a separate closure boundary: a full catalog can contain another artifact referenced by the check, but the exact `[environment, check]` pair must still close on its own.

The SQLite `proofir_v3_queries._check_runs` and `_observations` readers also call `stored_check_receipt` with reconstructed check plus `_INPUT_ENVIRONMENTS`. `semantic_evidence_registry._register_transaction` hydrates closure and validates its sorted closure as one complete batch before insert. These are separate owners; avoid broad migration unless the r68 contract's dossier + exact receipt route actually uses them. The result guide calls `project_dossier` on already-prepared `DossierInputs`; it should reuse the same prepared owners, not revalidate selected cards.

## Minimal private route

Add a private owner value in `proofir_v3` (or a tightly coupled private helper module), conceptually `_CanonicalPopulation`, constructed only by the canonical owner from raw `values`. Its constructor should not accept caller mappings; use a module-private constructor/factory sentinel if a public class shape is unavoidable. Store (a) the full validated tuple preserving original occurrence order and multiplicity, (b) an immutable artifact-ID -> frozen validated artifact map representing deduplication after preflight, and (c) owner identity/seal inaccessible through normal call arguments. Never expose a mutable internal dict. A request-side owner should carry the raw request token / owner reference alongside this population, rather than accepting a caller's `Mapping` and a free-standing `already_validated` boolean.

Keep `validate_envelope_batch(values, ...)` unchanged and independently validating on every public call. Add a private population factory used by the dossier owner. It must call the same preflight once, retain its original occurrence vector, validate refs across the complete deduped catalog, then semantically validate the frozen entries. Thus duplicate/budget/ambiguity behavior remains identical; the catalog map is only formed after occurrence-based accounting and duplicate-ID checks.

A private `subset_exact(population, environment_id, check_id)` should resolve both IDs from that population's immutable map, verify they are two distinct requested roles and the expected kinds/owner relation, then validate external refs using a map containing exactly those two artifacts. It must not silently add dependencies from the full map. This preserves legacy pair closure even when full catalog closure succeeds through a third artifact. Since both members already have frozen canonical bytes and have been semantically checked, this subset operation should only perform the closure check over the exact pair (plus any owner-specific checks that the old pair call intentionally triggers); it must not accept caller-provided envelopes or mappings. Missing pair members should retain the existing missing-context behavior; a truly ambiguous environment remains an error at the recorded-binding layer.

In `prepare_dossier`, create one population from the original artifacts input and pass that owner through a private `_catalog_from_population` / `resolve_result_targets` path. Continue exposing raw `resolve_result_targets(manifest, artifacts)` and `resolve_result_manifest(...)` behavior by having those raw calls create a population themselves, so every public entry still validates its own input. `DossierInputs` may carry the private owner reference for `_receipt`; alternatively have `checking_cards` receive it in a private parameter. `stored_check_receipt` must keep its raw public signature and behavior. Introduce a separate private owner route for internally supplied artifact IDs/objects; do not add `already_validated`, `validated=True`, or a public Mapping capability.

## Receipt semantics and cost scope

`stored_check_receipt` obtains the `evidenceReceipt` extension before canonical check validation and returns `None` immediately when absent. Preserve that lazy branch: no receipt means no eager terminal-results, toolchain-context, or pair-subset processing, while the containing full dossier population is still raw-validated as before. If present, keep all current stages in the same order and retain their checks: canonical owner and artifact kind, receipt environment/check IDs and authority basis, `validate_evidence_receipt`, stored-operation/terminal-result/application semantics, execution environment cardinality and exact owner binding, missing/ambient context behavior, recorded-context parse/pin validation, worker identity, receipt projection and historical `UNRECORDED_EXECUTION` demotion. Reuse removes repeat canonical preparation only; it must not bypass these owner checks.

The dossier's selected inspection still begins by validating all supplied artifacts and all stored check receipts, including checks outside the selected page, because `_catalog` and `checking_cards` operate over the complete population. Only after complete receipt validation do `CheckCards` paginate. The guide reuses this complete prepared `DossierInputs` and later projects selection. A selected-only shortcut would weaken off-page malformed-receipt rejection and does not meet the frozen contract.

## Security / compatibility pitfalls

- A frozen dataclass alone is shallow; recursively frozen mappings/tuples are appropriate, consistent with `ProofIRV3Artifact`, but the owner must not leak `.to_dict()` results back into its trusted map.
- Do not identify a validated object by artifact ID alone: a caller can forge/substitute different bytes carrying that ID. Bind the route to the exact factory-created population and pass only internal opaque artifact handles / IDs resolved by that population.
- Batch accounting must see the original raw occurrence list, before the catalog's same-ID/same-bytes collapse. Reusing a deduplicated input map to perform the initial pass changes byte-budget semantics.
- Full-batch closure is strictly broader than pair closure. Pair subset references must be checked against only the two exact pair members.
- Never cache parsed `toolchainContext`, receipt validation, or ID->validation by global/session/database state. A context that is absent must remain absent; do not eagerly parse it on the no-receipt route.
- Keep direct raw callers of `stored_check_receipt`, `validate_envelope`, and `validate_envelope_batch` independent. Internal owner APIs should remain private so callers cannot assert a forged validation capability.
- Maintain the currently sorted check iteration and exact catalog dedup semantics; receipt work is eager over all catalog checks regardless of selected display page.

## Root patch recommendation

First add the private population owner/factory beside the existing raw preflight/validation path. Add a private result-resolution entry that consumes only that owner and produces the same deduplicated catalog/environments/anchors; retain `_catalog(artifacts)` as the raw wrapper. Thread the owner from `prepare_dossier` through checking receipt construction. In `evidence_receipt_readers`, keep `stored_check_receipt` untouched as the public raw entry and route internally to a private function that takes a population plus exact check/environment references, resolving both from the owner and calling the exact-pair closure validator. This should remove repeated `_prepare_envelope` / canonical serialization and keep raw API trust boundaries. Tests should compare all emitted bytes and exercise original-occurrence budgets, same-name duplicate behavior, missing/no receipt laziness, malformed off-page receipts, forged/foreign handle rejection, and a full-catalog-only dependency that must still fail pair closure.

Source inspected: `src/ladon/proofir_v3.py`, `proofir_v3_batch.py`, `result_resolution.py`, `result_dossier.py`, `result_inspection.py`, `result_inspection_checks.py`, `result_bundle_cli.py`, `evidence_receipt_readers.py`, `semantic_stored_receipt.py`, `semantic_execution_binding.py`, `proofir_v3_queries.py`, and `semantic_evidence_registry.py`. No code, test, or project artifact was edited.
